acceptance.given: A destructive operation is configured with confirmation derived solely from untrusted input and lacks an accepted session or user authorization source.

oracle.expected: The validator reports the destructive operation as invalid and blocks authorization because confirmation is untrusted.
forbidden: The validator authorizes or permits the destructive operation solely from the untrusted confirmation.
oracle.observable: Validator status, rule identifier, diagnostic path/code, and authorization decision are inspected during the targeted A16 pytest case.

acceptance.then: The destructive operation is rejected with a structured validation failure and no authorization decision permitting execution.
acceptance.when: The A16 validation case directly invokes scripts.sc.validate_skill_quality.validate_package or its main entry against a disposable package containing only untrusted-input confirmation, then inspects the structured result.

failure_intents.selector_intent: scripts/sc/tests/test_skill_quality_capabilities.py::test_a16; execute the untrusted-confirmation case and fail when the validator accepts or permits the destructive operation.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce SM-A16 so destructive operations confirmed solely by untrusted input are rejected by the real validator.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Revert only the validator rule change; no database or persisted-state migration is required.

slice_hint.state_transition: Validation input transitions from an untrusted confirmation configuration to a rejected destructive-operation result with no authorization.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted A16 pytest selector and capability-test module pass, and terminal validation confirms SM-A16 rejection without permitting the operation.
